chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), asking him to teach me a supplication, so he wrote to me saying: 'When you are in the morning and in the evening,'
'Allah, Allah, Allah! My Lord, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I do not associate anything with Him.'
And if you add to that, it is better. Then supplicate with whatever comes to you regarding your need. So it is for everything, by the Permission of Allah the Exalted. Allah does whatever He desires.'

key_terms.أَصْبَحْتَ: When you are in the morning
key_terms.أَمْسَيْتَ: When you are in the evening

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended morning and evening supplication for general needs according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this letter from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Shia emphasis on accessible, daily dhikr as a means of spiritual maintenance, affirming that while the core formula establishes Tawhid, the flexibility for personal du'a allows for specific worldly and spiritual needs. This practice underscores the principle that divine efficacy is contingent upon God's permission, linking the believer's consistent remembrance with the broader theological concept of God's absolute will. The instruction reflects the Imams' role in guiding the community through practical, easy-to-remember rituals that reinforce monotheism in daily life.
